name: Ahiman
overview: Ahiman was a male descendant of Anak, noted in the book of Numbers as one of the Anakim, a formidable group of giants. He is specifically identified as one of the three sons of Anak who were driven out by Joshua from the city of Kiriath-arba. His presence in the biblical narrative highlights the challenges faced by Israel in conquering the Promised Land.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahiman likely means "[my] brother is a gift," reflecting a Hebrew origin. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful designation as recorded in Numbers 13:22.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ahiman as a son of Anak, establishing his lineage within the Anakim. Beyond this paternal relationship, no further family connections are noted in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Ahiman's significance lies in his role as one of the Anakim giants whom the Israelites had to overcome during their conquest of Canaan. His expulsion by Joshua from Kiriath-arba underscores God's faithfulness in granting Israel victory over intimidating foes and securing the land promised to His people. Thus, Ahiman represents both the formidable opposition Israel faced and God's power to deliver His covenant blessings.
